To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combined action of two T4SS effectors promotes invasome‐dependent uptake in ECs and epithelial cells.
the combined action of two T4SS effectors, BepC and BeF, triggers invasome formation on HeLa and HUVEC cells.
the combined action of two Bep proteins, BepC and BeFP, is sufficient to trigger invasomes and that BepC‐ and BepF ‐triggered invasomes are mechanistically distinct from BepG ‐triggered invasions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the combined action of two Bhe effectors that triggers invasome formation on ECs and HeLa cells.
the discovery of new Bhe effectors that promote invasome formation and the description of a new cell system to study this phenomenon.
a novel entry route into host cells and the identification of new effector proteins involved in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BepG and BepC/BepF trigger invasome‐dependent internalization of Bartonella hemselae by different mechanisms, and both mechanisms are required to fully mimic the natural infection process of Bhe in human endothelial and epithelia cells.
BepC, BepF and BepG trigger invasome‐associated uptake by different mechanisms.

the type IV secretion system of Bhe promotes invasome‐based entry into host cells by a combined action of the effector proteins Bhe BepC and/or Bhe BepF, and this process is distinct from the BepG‐mediated pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined action of effector proteins Bhe BepC and F is sufficient to trigger invasomes on ECs and HeLa cells.
BepC, BepF and BepG are the three major effector proteins that trigger invasome‐dependent uptake of Bhe in human cells.
the combined action of at least two different T4SS effectors is required to promote invasome formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined action of different T4SS‐delivered effectors can trigger invasome‐dependent uptake of Bhe.
BepC/BepF‐trigger invasomes are a novel entry mode of Bhe and that BepC‐ and BepF-triggered invasome‐formation differs from BepA‐ and BepG-triggered invasomes.
